The remaining parcel of the five, mentioned above, will be converted to a city park or open space area. Since this section of the project is located in a low lying area, subject to frequent flooding, clearance and redevelopment as a park with no permanent structures is an appropriate use for the land.
Two other areas of the project will be converted from residential use to park area, or parking area. These smaller neighborhood service areas will help in decreasing the density of the block between Second and Green Streets and Muench and Keller Streets and the block between Second and Green Streets and McLay and Peffer Streets.
Approximately 20 other parcels throughout the project area (see appendix G) will be converted from their present use, i.e., dense residential (zoned R-5), commercial or business, to single family residential. This action will "thin-out" the dense occupancy of general project area.
The remaining redevelopment is that of one parcel of neighborhood shopping area. As seen in appendix C, this parcel is located toward the southern end of the project along Second Street. This area will provide shopping to replace some of the existing neighborhood stores that will be acquired in the redevelopment of the various parcels throughout the project. These new developments will have its own parking area and will conform to the flood plain ordinances and associated building regulation.
When the project is completed, 119 of the 1,002 structures that existed at the beginning of the project activity will have been cleared. The land on which the acquired buildings stood will have been redeveloped or sold for redevelopment in accordance with the various land uses described above. The net effect on the total population of the project is not known since there is no satisfactory way of determining the number of people that will occupy the property scheduled for development as multi-family residential, along Front Street. There is also an uncertainty as to the number of families that will relocate in the project area after their properties have been acquired.
The best estimation is that the total overall population figures for the project will remain about the same due to the two countervailing factors of density reduction and redevelopment reacting against one another. All that can be anticipated at this time, using as a basis the proposed plan for the project area, is that if implementation occurs as intended, there will be a certain population redistributions between and within the various existing neighborhood areas of the project.
3. Treatment of Streets
